ideas: Avoiding debt and bad spending habits
Preparing for adult life and independence
Parents may not teach it at home

phrases.meaning: have enough money for basic needs
a useful skill for real life
prepare someone well for the future

model: Yes, I strongly believe schools should teach financial skills. First, it would help young people avoid serious money problems. Many young adults fall into debt because nobody has ever taught them how credit cards or loans work. I learned the hard way myself. When I got my first job, I used to spend most of my salary on eating out and shopping, and I would often struggle to make ends meet by the end of the month. A simple lesson at school on budgeting would have saved me a lot of stress. Another reason is that not every family talks about money. My parents were great, but they never explained how to put money aside or invest. A class on these topics would teach a practical skill that everyone needs, whatever job they do. Now I no longer live beyond my means, but it took me years to learn to manage my money properly. So overall, teaching financial skills early could set students up for life.
